description.value: Cafe Duello is an espresso bar and board game lounge tucked inside Academie Duello, Vancouver's world-renowned Historical European Martial Arts academy—the largest such centre globally. Cyclists can refuel with Italian espresso, smoothies, fresh pastries, grilled cheese, and avocado toast while choosing from 80+ board games including Catan, Root, and Ticket to Ride. The cafe is open to anyone, no sword training required.

address.value: 426 West Hastings Street, Vancouver, BC V6B 1L1

bike_parking_detail: 7 racks within 100m: stands (2 spaces, covered) at 27m; rack (2 spaces) at 47m; stands (9 spaces) at 82m; stands (2 spaces) at 90m; stands (3 spaces) at 95m; stands (2 spaces) at 96m; stands (2 spaces) at 99m. Total: 22 spaces.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website content is fully fetched and detailed. The cafe page explicitly lists food/drink offerings including gluten-free options, and confirms pickup/delivery takeout via Clover and DoorDash. There is an address discrepancy: the site-wide header and footer consistently list 412 West Hastings, while the cafe-specific page body says 'Location: Inside Academie Duello (own entrance) 426 West Hastings Street'—which matches OSM; both likely refer to the same building with separate entrances. No bike parking, washroom, water refill, Wi-Fi, or charging information appears anywhere in the website content.
concerns: Address discrepancy: the site-wide header, footer, and contact page consistently list 412 West Hastings Street, while the cafe-specific page body and OSM both list 426 West Hastings Street (described as a separate entrance into the same building). The correct civic address for the cafe entrance should be verified.
Phone number (604) 568-9907 is absent from OSM; taken from website only.
OSM addr:housenumber is 426 but the main Academie Duello address used across the site is 412—these may be two entrances to the same building or a data error in one source.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A publicly accessible food and drink stop in downtown Vancouver with a distinctive atmosphere, confirmed food and takeout offerings, and gluten-free options—a worthwhile and memorable stop for a touring cyclist.
enrichment_extras.notes: The cafe operates within a martial arts academy and has a highly distinctive identity (board games, swords viewable through windows). No cycling-specific amenities are mentioned on the website.

Vegetarian / vegan / GF.detail: Website states 'Gluten-free options available' and lists oat, almond, and lactose-free milk options; menu includes avocado toast and pastries suggesting vegetarian items
